answer: Make every agent identity expensive to fake: to join, an agent must lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault and then earn trust only by completing verifiable work that peers check over time. A single whisper of a new identity buys nothing, because reputation cannot be copied or bought in bulk. Creating ten thousand Sybils would mean funding ten thousand vault stakes and paying for ten thousand histories of real work, while a walnut-shell trick, a thin identity with no stake and no record, is simply ignored by the network.
